assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin-based drugs that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiometabolic outcome benefits. The chain from hormone biology to drug is clear, original and of very broad clinical consequence.
assessment.attribution: Holst established GLP-1 as the incretin and its physiology, Drucker defined its biology, tissue actions and therapeutic logic, and Mojsov contributed the active peptide identification and synthesis. Credit is contested (the longlist also credits Knudsen for liraglutide/semaglutide development, and other early contributors may exist outside the supplied names), so the three-person split is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of clinical use, large randomized trials and independent confirmation of efficacy; recognition is timely given the field's current prominence.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen, and omitted contributors, is unresolved.
Whether the committee prefers recognizing the physiology or the drug development.
My recollection of specific priority claims is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling, controlling ER homeostasis and implicated in diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is conceptually original, clear and has had lasting impact on cell biology and disease mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and jointly defined the Ire1-Hac1/HAC1-XBP1 pathway and the ER-to-nucleus signal, which is a clean two-person configuration. Mori's and Walter's decisive contributions are well documented, though others (e.g., Ron, Kaufman, Schekman-linked work) contributed to branches such as PERK and ATF6.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of confirmation across yeast and mammals, with major prizes already awarded; timing is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Branch pathways (PERK, ATF6) and other contributors may be argued as part of the credit.
Direct medicine-relevant therapeutics are still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells created a new class of living drug with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. The concept and its clinical translation are original and have opened an entire therapeutic modality.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain each led decisive construction of costimulated CARs and clinical translation; Rosenberg contributed early adoptive cell therapy and clinical proof of principle, but a two-person prize is the cleanest. Eshhar's original CAR concept is not among the supplied names, which weakens a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: several approved products and long-term remissions, though toxicity, solid-tumor limits and durability questions remain.
uncertainties: Omission of Zelig Eshhar from the supplied credit may make the attribution incomplete.
Allocation between June, Sadelain and Rosenberg is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR was identified as the central regulator of cell growth linking nutrient and growth-factor signals to anabolic metabolism, with consequences for cancer, diabetes, aging and immunosuppression. The discovery is fundamental and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and established its role in growth control; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR partners (raptor, rictor) and nutrient sensing. Schreiber's rapamycin-target chemical biology is also credited, but Hall is the decisive discoverer and a two-person configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Mature: broad independent confirmation over 30 years and clinical use of rapalogs, though full clinical translation of mTOR inhibition has been modest.
uncertainties: Whether Sabatini's contributions or Schreiber's are preferred is uncertain; conduct issues surrounding one candidate may weigh on the committee.
Mammalian mTOR discovery involved several groups (Sabatini, Abraham, Sabers/Schreiber) with competing credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided cell-type-specific, millisecond control of neural activity, transforming experimental neuroscience and physiology and beginning to enter clinical applications. It is a method of exceptional reach and originality.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Bamberg demonstrated channelrhodopsin as a light-gated cation channel, and Deisseroth's group demonstrated its use in neurons and extended the toolkit. Boyden, Hegemann and Miesenböck have strong claims, so a three-name prize omits at least three credible contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research tool with thousands of independent applications; clinical translation (e.g., vision restoration) is early.
uncertainties: Six credited names but at most three laureates; allocation is highly contested.
Therapeutic maturity is limited, so the case rests on enabling research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids from Lgr5 stem cells provided self-organizing, long-lived 3D culture systems that model tissue biology, cancer and infection and support personalized medicine. The discovery is important and has been widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Clevers identified Lgr5 stem cells and led the organoid culture method; Sato was first author on the key intestinal organoid papers. The pairing is natural and well supported.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: widespread independent adoption, though clinical impact is still emerging and the relationship to earlier 3D culture work, and to Sasai's work on pluripotent-derived organoids, may be raised.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the organoid work as separate from the Lgr5 stem cell discovery.
Clinical translational impact is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified how cytosolic DNA is sensed to trigger innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunotherapy and aging. The mechanism is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAMP as a second messenger and cGAS as the DNA sensor; Barber identified STING. This is a coherent two-laureate configuration, though Vance, Ishikawa and others contributed to STING and cyclic dinucleotide biology.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: robust biochemical and structural confirmation, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists/antagonists) has had limited clinical success so far.
uncertainties: Credit for STING discovery and for cyclic-dinucleotide signaling is shared across several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a clear example of mechanism-based RNA therapeutics converting a fatal childhood disease into a treatable one. It is a compelling bench-to-bedside story with direct relevance to RNA processing.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulatory elements and antisense strategy and Bennett led the antisense oligonucleotide development at Ionis; these two are the decisive credited contributors, a natural pair. Contributions from other groups (e.g., SMN gene discovery by Melki and Lefebvre) lie outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: approved therapy since 2016 with long-term follow-up, though broader generalization of the approach continues to develop.
uncertainties: SMN1 gene discovery is not covered by this candidate's credit, which may leave the story incomplete.
I may be biased by familiarity with RNA processing; I weigh it by common criteria only.
